title: G-rings ascend along weakly etale Noetherian ring maps
statement: Let $A$ and $B$ be commutative Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and let $f:A\to B$ be weakly etale [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. If $A$ is a G-ring [def-weil-pbc-g-ring], then $B$ is a G-ring.

source.document: Silvio Greco, Two theorems on excellent rings, Nagoya Mathematical Journal 60 (1976), 139–149, DOI 10.1017/S0027763000017190
source.place: Theorem 5.3(i), with P = geometrically regular in Section 1.1; Remark 5.2 identifies the AF hypothesis with weak etaleness for Noetherian rings. Printed pp. 139–140, 146–147 (PDF pp. 1–2, 8–9). G-ring terminology: Stacks Tag 07GH (definition-G-ring).

proof.text: At a prime q of B, localize f at p = f⁻¹(q) to g : R = A_p → S = B_q. The localized rings are Noetherian local rings and g is flat and local [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-ring-maps]. Weak etaleness of A → S follows by localization and composition. Descend its two flatness conditions to R using Module.flat_iff_of_isLocalization and the tensor equivalence Algebra.TensorProduct.equivOfCompatibleSMul; multiplication commutes with that equivalence. This uses the two-flatness definition [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra].

source.place: Algebra.WeaklyEtale.trans, base-change instance, of_isLocalization; Mathlib.RingTheory.Flat.Localization, Module.flat_iff_of_isLocalization.

proof.text: The closed fibre F = κ(R) ⊗_R S is weakly etale, hence absolutely flat by Ring.AbsolutelyFlat.of_flat_lmul' (Stacks 092I). As the residue-field tensor product of a local map it is local (TensorProduct.isLocalRing), and hence a field. By [lem-weil-pbc-weakly-etale-field-separable], F/κ(R) is separable algebraic; [lem-exc-separable-algebraic-square-zero-lifting] makes it formally etale. Transport ordinary formal smoothness along Algebra.TensorProduct.quotIdealMapEquivQuotTensor to S/m_R S. Every square-zero lifting problem therefore lifts, including the continuous ones, proving [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic] for the closed fibre.

source.document: Stacks Project, More on Algebra; Mathlib.RingTheory.Etale.Field

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-flat-formally-smooth-closed-fibre-adic] on g and step 2, and then [lem-weil-pbc-fs-adic-complete-source-target], to obtain ψ : R̂ → Ŝ and its adic formal smoothness. Its quotient-coordinate formula proves ψ ∘ u = v ∘ g by AdicCompletion.ext_evalₐ. AdicCompletion.maximalIdeal_eq_map together with this square shows ψ maps the maximal ideal into the maximal ideal, so it is local. The completions are complete local rings by Mathlib.RingTheory.AdicCompletion.LocalRing and Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian]. Rewrite the extended target ideal as its maximal ideal and apply [lem-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-complete-local-regular] to make ψ regular.

source.document: Silvio Greco, Two theorems on excellent rings; Stacks Project, More on Algebra

proof.text: The G-ring assumption makes u : R → R̂ regular [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]. All fibres of the Noetherian ring Ŝ are Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-noetherian], so [lem-weil-pbc-regular-composition] applies to u and ψ and proves regularity of h = v ∘ g.

source.document: Silvio Greco, Two theorems on excellent rings; Stacks Project, More on Algebra

proof.text: Fix a prime s of S and let t be its contraction to R. Put k = κ(t), L = κ(s), F = k ⊗_R S. Construct ε : F → L from the residue-field map and S → L. It is surjective on stalks because its composite with S → F is S → L, which is surjective on stalks. F is absolutely flat by the weakly-etale base-change instance and Ring.AbsolutelyFlat.of_flat_lmul'. Prove L is the localization of F at ker ε: denominators map to nonzero elements; stalk surjectivity gives fractions; for ε(x)=ε(y), choose b with x-y=(x-y)²b and use 1-(x-y)b, whose image is 1, to annihilate x-y. Localization and composition make k → L weakly etale. By [lem-weil-pbc-weakly-etale-field-separable], L/k is separable algebraic. This replaces the finite-product decomposition of the original route.

source.document: Stacks Project, More on Algebra; Mathlib.RingTheory.LocalRing.ResidueField and Mathlib.RingTheory.LocalProperties.Surjective

proof.text: Put C = Ŝ, D = k ⊗_R C, E = F ⊗_S C and Q = L ⊗_S C. Algebra.IsPushout.cancelBaseChangeAlg identifies E with D, the tensor cancellation of [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-cancel-base-change]. Transport the geometric regularity of D supplied by step 4 to E using [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-regularity-field-iso]. Base change of the localization ε identifies Q as a localization of E (IsLocalization.tensorProduct_tensorProduct). To prove geometric regularity survives this localization, first localize Noetherianity. The geometric_localization helper allows the localized target to inhabit a larger universe; the finite-field-extension theorem handles the resulting larger universe of test fields. For each finite purely inseparable K/k, use [lem-weil-pbc-geometrically-regular-finitely-generated-extensions] to make K ⊗_k E regular, and use IsLocalization.tensorProduct_tensorProduct_right and [lem-weil-pbc-localization-of-regular-ring] to make K ⊗_k Q regular. This proves geometric regularity of Q over k. It is Noetherian also by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-noetherian]. Apply the forward implication [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-regularity-separable-extension-forward] along L/k from step 5 to obtain geometric regularity over L.

source.document: Silvio Greco, Two theorems on excellent rings; Stacks Project, Algebra
source.place: Theorem 5.3(i), formal-fibre argument, implemented by localization instead of a finite product; Tags 0381 and 07QH; Mathlib.RingTheory.Localization.BaseChange.

proof.text: The completion map v : S → Ŝ is flat by AdicCompletion.flat_of_isNoetherian (the flatness clause of [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-faithfully-flat]). Its fibres at all primes s are geometrically regular by step 6, so v is regular. Since q was arbitrary and B is Noetherian, [def-weil-pbc-g-ring] concludes IsGRing B. If B has no primes the condition is vacuous.
